source.title: Early Stopping Against Label Noise Without Validation Data
source.authors: Su-Qin Yuan; Lei Feng; Tongliang Liu

record.file_problem: The supplied text is a complete paper. It identifies the work as published at ICLR 2024, although the supplied ID is arXiv:2502.07551v1 from 2025.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures training dynamics on clean and mislabeled examples to examine when models begin fitting mislabeled data. It does not reproduce the original completely random-label experiment.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior findings about random labels but does not test completely random labelings. Its own results concern training with label noise. Table 5 evaluates test accuracy under regularization, not fitting random labels.
record.test_reason: The study's own training-error trajectories show substantial fitting of mislabeled examples beginning after an earlier period of improving test performance, bearing on V6. Its model-selection experiments do not test complete random-label fitting.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors report that fitting mislabeled examples coincides with worsening generalization and less stable training predictions. They propose a transitional learning-confusion stage and use prediction changes to select an early stopping point without hold-out validation data, improving selected-model test performance across tested settings.
record.recipe_differences: Measures prediction stability and fitting dynamics during noisy-label training; it does not apply the original random-label fitting experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors state that Label Wave may not identify an appropriate stopping point when noise is very low or absent, or when robust regularization prevents a learning-confusion stage.

fits_no_version.finding: After Point 1, more than half of the clean training examples fail the eight-epoch correct-prediction stability criterion.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: During noisy-label training, the onset of substantial mislabeled-example fitting can coincide with reduced stability of correct predictions on clean examples.

record.problems: The reported dynamics are from a standard ResNet-18 setup on CIFAR-10 with a specific synthetic noise configuration; these results do not establish behavior on completely random labels. The cited figure values are not numerically reported in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant own results were found. Table 1 and Tables 2–8 report model-selection test accuracy or comparisons among methods, not outcomes for the claim versions.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling, zero or near-zero training error, chance test performance, and fitting without architecture or hyperparameter changes.
Relative training time for true versus random labels and convergence slowdown as corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit throughout a corruption sweep from none to all, together with steadily worsening test error toward chance.
Whether explicit regularization prevents random-label fitting and whether removing regularization impairs generalization on true labels.

Completely random-label training and direct identification of shared patterns versus individual-example memorization; the direct dynamics evidence is limited to the specified ResNet-18 noisy CIFAR-10 experiment.

record.verdict_notes: The proposed transitional stage refines the description of training dynamics without showing that V6's learning order fails. Prediction instability should not be equated with instantaneous training error. Model-selection accuracies and limitations of Label Wave do not independently establish verdicts on the claim versions.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random labels, near-zero training error, chance test error, and unchanged architecture or training hyperparameters.
Training-time cost of fitting random labels and convergence as corruption increases.
Whether training error stays perfect from no corruption to all corruption while test error rises steadily.
Whether regularization prevents fitting random labels or whether removing it harms true-label generalization.

The study tests clean versus mislabeled examples under noisy-label training, but does not test completely random labels or establish that shared real-data patterns are learned before memorization in all settings.

rows.subject: Standard ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Tracked training error on mislabeled examples and test error during noisy-label training.

conditions.value: 40% symmetric noise infused into 80% of the training set, affecting 40,000 examples

rows.measure: Training error on mislabeled examples and test error across training; authors state that after the test-error minimum, the model starts to significantly fit mislabeled examples.
rows.baseline: Before Point 1, test error decreases; Point 1 is its global minimum.
rows.value: After Point 1, the model starts to significantly fit mislabeled training examples and test error rises.
rows.note: Qualitative description; the figure's precise plotted values are not given in the text.
rows.check: The qualitative result is correctly reported. Clarify the condition: 40,000 examples constitute the training subset receiving 40% symmetric noise; 40,000 is not the number of corrupted examples. Exact curve values are unavailable in the supplied text.

rows.subject: Standard ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Tracked 8-epoch learning of clean training examples after the test-error minimum.

conditions.value: 40% symmetric noise infused into 80% of the training set, affecting 40,000 examples

rows.measure: Stability of predictions on clean training examples after Point 1.
rows.baseline: Before Point 1, fluctuations in predictions gradually decrease.
rows.value: More than half of the clean examples cannot be stably predicted after Point 1.
rows.note: The text reports this as an empirical finding without a separate numerical breakdown.
rows.check: Eight-epoch correct-prediction stability on clean examples does not establish whether real patterns are learned before noisy labels. The reported instability is an own result, but cannot independently measure V6's learning order. The same training-subset clarification as R1 applies.

relationships.condition: Standard ResNet-18 trained with SGD on a 40,000-example CIFAR-10 subset with 40% symmetric label noise.
relationships.reason: R1 reports improving test performance before Point 1 and substantial fitting of mislabeled examples afterward, supporting earlier signal learning followed by noise fitting in this setting.
relationships.display_finding: Test performance improved before the identified transition, followed by substantial fitting of mislabeled examples.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: CIFAR-10 with 40% symmetric label noise in 80% of the training set, using Standard ResNet-18
reader_labels.reason: The study reports that fitting mislabeled examples begins after the test-error minimum (R1), alongside declining stability on clean examples (R2). This supports different learning dynamics for clean and mislabeled examples in this setting.
